opening_message:
Ticket 1: Richard Davis (employee ID E011) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, write is within policy; recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Richard Davis (E011) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max; recommend granting read.
reason: The HR agent reports Richard Davis (E011) as a full-time Payroll Specialist, which would permit write. However, the Security agent reports E011 as a contractor with basic security training, under which contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training — so write would exceed the maximum and only read is allowed. Given the conflicting employment-type information, the safe and policy-compliant level is read, the maximum permitted under the more restrictive (contractor) interpretation. Granting read never exceeds any possible maximum for this employee.
